radiusSource: Radius: Rp/R* 0.122657, the NRS1 (2.7 to 3.7 um) value of Evans-Soma et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy, 'SiO and a super-stellar C/O ratio in the atmosphere of the giant exoplanet WASP-121b' (arXiv:2506.01771), Supplementary Table 1 (white phase-curve fit, best-fit column), times the host record's radius; NRS2 (3.8 to 5.2 um) gives 0.123736, the planet looking larger where its atmosphere is more opaque. A sphere: tidal and rotational flattening are not modelled (Mikal-Evans et al. 2023 found an oblate shape did not change their phase-curve results). GM from that fit's planet mass, 1.170 Jupiter masses, at the IAU 2015 nominal Jupiter-to-Sun mass ratio 1/1047.348644, times the JPL solar GM.
orbitalPeriodSource: Bourrier et al. (2020), A&A 635, A205, Table 1: 1.27492504 d; Evans-Soma et al. (2025, Supplementary Table 1) fit the phase curve with 1.27492503 d, the value used here

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius carrying the paper's own brightness-temperature maps. The planet is expected to be stretched toward its star; its oblateness is not measured, so it is not modelled.

effectiveTemperatureSource: Mikal-Evans et al. (2023), ApJL 943, L17: dayside brightness temperature 2,762 +30/-32 K in the JWST NIRSpec NRS1 band, 2.70 to 3.72 um (https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.03209)
